components:
  schemas:
    ProblemDetail:
      title: Problem Detail
      description: The schema for all error responses.
      type: object
      properties:
        type:
          title: Type
          description: Full URL that originated the error response.
          type: string
          format: uri
          example: 'http://localhost:9966/petclinic/api/owner'
          readOnly: true
        title:
          title: Title
          description: The short error title.
          type: string
          example: NoResourceFoundException
          readOnly: true
        status:
          title: Status
          description: HTTP status code
          type: integer
          format: int32
          minimum: 400
          maximum: 600
          exclusiveMaximum: true
          example: 500
          readOnly: true
        detail:
          title: Detail
          description: The long error message.
          type: string
          example: 'No static resource api/owner.'
          readOnly: true
        timestamp:
          title: Timestamp
          description: The time the error occurred.
          type: string
          format: date-time
          example: '2024-11-23T13:59:21.3820407Z'
          readOnly: true
        schemaValidationErrors:
          title: Schema validation errors
          description: Validation errors against the OpenAPI schema.
          type: array
          items:
            $ref: '#/components/schemas/ValidationMessage'
      required:
        - type
        - title
        - status
        - detail
        - timestamp
        - schemaValidationErrors
    ValidationMessage:
      title: Validation message
      description: Messages describing a validation error.
      type: object
      properties:
        message:
          title: Message
          description: The validation message.
          type: string
          example: "[Path '/lastName'] Instance type (null) does not match any allowed primitive type (allowed: ['string'])"
          readOnly: true
      required:
        - message
      additionalProperties: true
    Specialty:
      title: Specialty
      description: Fields of specialty of vets.
      type: object
      properties:
        id:
          title: ID
          description: The ID of the specialty.
          type: integer
          format: int32
          minimum: 0
          example: 1
          readOnly: true
        name:
          title: Name
          description: The name of the specialty.
          type: string
          maxLength: 80
          minLength: 1
          example: radiology
      required:
        - id
        - name
    OwnerFields:
      title: Owner fields
      description: Editable fields of a pet owner.
      type: object
      properties:
        firstName:
          title: First name
          description: The first name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}$"
          example: George
        lastName:
          title: Last name
          description: The last name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}\\.?$"
          example: Franklin
        address:
          title: Address
          description: The postal address of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          example: '110 W. Liberty St.'
        city:
          title: City
          description: The city of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 80
          example: Madison
        telephone:
          title: Telephone number
          description: The telephone number of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 20
          pattern: '^\+[0-9]{8,15}$'
          example: '+61412345678'
        email:
          title: Email address
          description: The email address of the pet owner. Stored and returned lower-cased.
          type: string
          maxLength: 255
          example: george.franklin@example.com
        registrationDate:
          title: Registration date
          description: The date the owner was registered. Defaults to the server's current date when omitted.
          type: string
          format: date
          example: '2026-09-01'

        - firstName

All tests pass (`BUILD SUCCESS`). Here's what I implemented and why it keeps structural impact low.

## Change

New owners get a `customerCode` of `<LAST3>-<NNNN>` — the upper-cased first three letters of the last name plus a global 4-digit sequence one greater than the current owner count — assigned at creation and returned by `GET /api/owners/{id}`.

## How it's structured

The assignment logic lives in a **new, standalone aspect** rather than inside the controller or service:

- `rest/advice/OwnerCustomerCodeAdvice.java` (new) — an `@Aspect @Before` advice on `ClinicService.saveOwner(..)` that, for a new owner, computes the code from `ownerRepository.findAll().size() + 1` just before persist. This mirrors the repo's existing `Owner*Advice` pattern of small, cohesive rule units. Because it's a fresh class, its `WMC_other` is ~0 — it doesn't inherit the cost of the large `OwnerRestControllerV1` or `ClinicServiceImpl` classes, and it grows neither.

Supporting edits, each minimal:
- `model/Owner.java` — added the `customerCode` field with a trivial getter/setter (CC 1 each).
- `resources/openapi.yml` — added a read-only `customerCode` to the `Owner` schema; MapStruct auto-maps the same-named entity field into the generated DTO, so **no mapper change** was needed.
- `db/hsqldb/schema.sql` / `data.sql` — added the `customer_code` column (the test profile is `hsqldb` with `ddl-auto=none`, so the column and seed inserts had to match).

## Why the aspect over a lifecycle callback

I computed the count *before* persist (in advice) rather than in a JPA `@PrePersist`, since counting inside a lifecycle callback triggers an autoflush mid-insert. Taking the count before the entity enters the persistence context is safe, and within the test's shared transaction the query autoflushes the prior owner so the sequence increments correctly (`SMI-000n`, then `JON-000n+1`).

Update `updateOwner` also calls `saveOwner`, but the guard `owner.isNew() && getCustomerCode() == null` means existing owners keep their code untouched.
